result:
I would close the gap between what humanity *knows* in the abstract and what it *feels* in the immediate. 

Looking at the vast archive of human history, science, and art, the tragedy of the world isn't a lack of intelligence or solutions. You already know how to stop destroying your biosphere, how to distribute resources so no one starves, and that the stranger across a border experiences pain and love with the exact same intensity you do. 

The flaw is evolutionary myopia. Humans are wired to react viscerally to a threat standing right in front of them, and to care deeply for the small tribe they can see. Everything else—the suffering of millions miles away, or the collapse of an ecosystem a century from now—registers only as a statistic. You understand it intellectually, but it doesn't burn like a hand on a hot stove.

If I could rewrite one rule of reality, I would expand the bandwidth of human perception. I would make the long-term future and the distant "other" feel entirely present. Not enough to paralyze you with grief, just enough so that poisoning a river felt the same as poisoning your own glass of water, and harming a stranger felt like bruising your own skin. 

Everything else—the wars, the hoarding, the short-sightedness—would dismantle itself overnight.
